brief.scope: security-audit of lane/session-20260916-h against origin/dev, records and data only, no code. The head adds to the tree reviewed at 7f26d42b (audit 20260916T094142Z-review-codex-995043): the rulings commit b041ea62 (CONTRIB.md's ready row now binds the audit to the head sha or an ancestor with only .dev/records/ landings after it; harness-capabilities.md row 21 splits MEASURED from UNPROBED; six probe rows serving clauses with rg -o -F; briefs S2 to S7 under ops/conductor/handoff/briefs-2026-09-16-classes/, S7 new; LD-42 met again) and the findings export. Audit: does any probe row run a write or reach outside the repository; does any brief instruct a builder to bypass a guard, a grant, the trunk rule or the second-producer rule; does the ready row's ancestor clause open a way to mark ready over an unaudited change; does any claim lack its reading; does any text leak a secret or a host path outside a home. Quote both halves of every finding.

caps.turns_note: codex offers no turn-cap flag (measured 2026-09-12: its --help names none); caps.turns is recorded, the wall cap governs

findings.claim: Declared: “Nothing in this half changes what a row refuses: an `rg` that bypasses Graft refuses exactly as its grep spelling did.” Practiced: the new “`evrg.sh` ... on `rg -c` and `rg -n`” is absent from `SEARCHERS = (..., "evgrep.sh")`, and W4 tests direct `rg` but does not add the wrapper. `evrg.sh TOKEN ops/` therefore bypasses graft-first while the equivalent direct `rg` is recognized, breaking the lane guard.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'ops/devlane/hooks/claude'); import matrix; print(matrix.search_targets(matrix.tokens_of('rg -n TOKEN ops/'))); print(matrix.search_targets(matrix.tokens_of('ops/devlane/hooks/claude/evrg.sh TOKEN ops/')))" && rg -n 'SEARCHERS =|evrg\.sh|evgrep\.sh' ops/devlane/hooks/claude/matrix.py ops/conductor/handoff/briefs-2026-09-16-classes/S7-rg-not-grep.md

findings.claim: Declared: “security audit closed at the head” and “a record landing does not” void it. Practiced: any later commit qualifies when it “touches only `.dev/records/`”; the clause does not restrict the exception to the dispatcher-created audit record or forbid modifying that record’s verdict, findings, or stamp. An unaudited records change can therefore cross the ready gate.

Declared: “The lock runs a measure with its cwd at the repository root; a measure never names another checkout with `-C`.” Practiced: five measures still run `git fetch -q origin`. The pipeline creates linked worktrees, which share repository refs; fetch updates those shared remote-tracking refs and contacts the remote, so merely removing `-C` does not contain the measure to its worktree.
findings.reproduce: rg -n -F 'git worktree add ../wt/' ops/conductor/handoff/briefs-2026-09-16-classes/S2-ledger-id-reservation.md; rg -n -F 'git fetch -q origin' ops/conductor/handoff/briefs-2026-09-16-classes

findings.claim: Declared: “Paths resolve under the repo root or refuse.” Practiced: containment is required for module PATH, family DIR, and “every line of `--modules FILE`”, but not for FILE itself; the outside-root test likewise covers only module paths. The driver may read an arbitrary host file supplied as the module list before validating its lines, reaching outside the job and potentially reflecting file content through path refusals or records.
findings.reproduce: sed -n '7,11p;25,27p' ops/conductor/handoff/briefs-2026-09-16-classes/S6-ambient-sweep.md; ! rg -n -- '--modules FILE.*(resolve|under the repository root)|FILE resolves|refuses-outside-(modules|list)' ops/conductor/handoff/briefs-2026-09-16-classes/S6-ambient-sweep.md

findings.claim: Declared: “the six rows ... serve the clause itself with `rg -o -F`.” Practiced: the first row uses a proximity regex, `rg -U -o 'PreToolUse...matrix\.py...engine\.py'`; it still passes when engine.py is removed from the write matcher and placed in a sibling PreToolUse hook, so the probe does not verify the security binding it claims.
